project: Weave AI News Ontology Dogfood Repair
description: Focused Ralph repair loop from Hermes dogfood of an AI News ontology E2E scenario. Fix issues found while creating ainews ontology, ingesting one week of AI news, and browsing/searching it in the WebUI. Follow TDD/BDD, add regression tests, run quality gates, commit one story per iteration.

userStories.name: Ensure imported ontology object indexes exist before accepted stream ingest
userStories.description: Hermes dogfood imported ontology `ainews` and immediately streamed 103 AI_News CREATE edits. Ingest returned 200 with edit counts, but list/search/aggregate failed with `index not found for object type "AI_News"` or showed zero rows. Manual index rebuild created an empty index (`indexedCount: 0`), and only a second ingest made data visible. Fix root cause so import/create-object-type bootstraps the index before ingest is accepted, or ingest fails fast instead of claiming success. Preferred behavior: import/create path creates the object index automatically and immediate ingest becomes visible without rebuild/reingest.
bdd_acceptance: Given a new ontology is imported with object type AI_News, When CREATE edits are immediately posted to /api/v2/ontologies/ainews/streams/AI_News/ingest, Then the accepted records become visible via GET /objects/AI_News without manual index rebuild.

Given import/create object type succeeds, When POST /api/v2/ontologies/ainews/objects/AI_News/search is called after ingest, Then it does not return IndexNotFound/SearchObjectsFailed for the new object type.
Given the index cannot be created, When stream ingest is requested, Then the API must fail fast with a non-2xx error and must not return an editCount success that later disappears.
Given an existing ontology is replaced or re-imported, When indexes are rebuilt/bootstraped, Then stale index state does not leak old rows and new ingests converge idempotently.
dogfood_evidence: First ingest returned 200 for 50+50+3 edits; list/search then returned `index not found for object type "AI_News"`.
POST /api/admin/indexes/rebuild returned scopedKey ainews__AI_News indexedCount 0; re-ingest after rebuild produced browser totalCount 103.
quality_gates: targeted backend regression test for import/create-object-type + immediate ingest/list/search red->green
targeted index bootstrap tests for replace/re-import if applicable
go test ./pkg/... or narrower package tests covering the changed code
Hermes/browser verification of /browser/ainews/AI_News totalCount 103 after a fresh import+single ingest

userStories.name: Fix BrowserPage full-text search contract for containsAnyTerm
userStories.description: On /browser/ainews/AI_News, typing OpenAI into Search objects and pressing Enter renders `INVALID_ARGUMENT: SearchObjectsFailed`. BrowserPage builds where `{type:'containsAnyTerm', field:'title', value:['OpenAI']}`, but the Go backend expects a string value and reports `containsAnyTerm value must be a string`. Align frontend/backend contract so browser search works for normal multi-term text.
bdd_acceptance: Given /browser/ainews/AI_News is loaded with 103 rows, When the user searches for OpenAI, Then matching rows are displayed and the UI does not show INVALID_ARGUMENT/SearchObjectsFailed.
Given BrowserPage submits a full-text search, Then the request body matches the backend where contract (no array/string mismatch).

Given a multi-word search such as `OpenAI Codex`, When submitted, Then backend semantics are correct and covered by tests (either one string accepted by backend or backend explicitly supports an array of terms).
Given the search API returns an error, Then the UI error should include the backend reason when available, not just `INVALID_ARGUMENT: SearchObjectsFailed`.
dogfood_evidence: Exact failing reason: `containsAnyTerm value must be a string: json: cannot unmarshal array into Go value of type string`.
quality_gates: frontend BDD/unit regression test for BrowserPage search request shape red->green
backend where-clause test if backend is changed
Hermes/browser verification: search OpenAI on /browser/ainews/AI_News returns rows

userStories.name: Render accurate Explorer property metadata flags
userStories.description: /explorer/ainews/AI_News properties table shows Searchable and Sortable as false for every field. Direct detailed properties API reports true for many fields, including title/category/deliveredDate/source/summary. Fix Explorer object type detail so Nullable/Searchable/Sortable reflect authoritative detailed property metadata rather than lossy objectType.properties map defaults.
bdd_acceptance: Given detailed property metadata marks title as searchable and sortable, When /explorer/ainews/AI_News renders, Then title shows Searchable ✓ and Sortable ✓.
Given detailed property metadata marks rank sortable but not searchable, When the properties table renders, Then rank shows Sortable ✓ and Searchable ✕.
Given detailed property metadata marks rawItem searchable but not sortable, When the properties table renders, Then rawItem shows Searchable ✓ and Sortable ✕.
Given the detailed properties request is loading or fails, Then the UI degrades explicitly (loading/error or unknown) rather than confidently showing all flags as false.
dogfood_evidence: API `/objectTypes/byRid/<rid>/properties` reports isSearchable/isSortable true while UI renders all ✕.
quality_gates: frontend BDD/unit regression test for ObjectType detail property flags red->green
